3.name: Spellcasting
3.notes:
You learn to cast spells using the Wizard spell list.

Cantrips. You know Mage Hand and two Wizard cantrips of your choice. Mage Hand cannot be replaced, but you may replace one other cantrip whenever you gain a Rogue level. At Rogue level 10, you learn an additional Wizard cantrip.

Spell Slots. You gain spell slots according to the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table and regain all expended slots after a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells. You prepare Wizard spells of level 1 or higher. You begin with three level 1 Wizard spells. You prepare additional spells as your Rogue level increases, according to the table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one prepared spell with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You may use an Arcane Focus for your spells.

3.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
3.notes: You can cast Mage Hand as a Bonus Action, and the spectral hand can be Invisible. You may control the hand as a Bonus Action, and you may use it to make Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks.

9.name: Magical Ambush
9.notes: If you have the Invisible condition when you cast a spell that targets a creature, that creature has Disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.

13.name: Versatile Trickster
13.notes: You can use your Mage Hand to distract enemies. When you use the Trip option of your Cunning Strike on a creature, you may also Trip another creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand.

17.name: Spell Thief
17.notes:
When a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area, you may take a Reaction to force it to make an Intelligence saving throw (DC = your spell save DC). On a failed save, the spell has no effect on you, and you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is level 1 or higher and of a level you can cast.

For the next 8 hours, you have the spell prepared and the original caster cannot cast it during that time.

Once you steal a spell, you cannot use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.
